newsitem.title: SPAIN: TABLE-Spain Repsol H1 results by division.
newsitem.headline: TABLE-Spain Repsol H1 results by division.

text.p: Spanish energy group Repsol six months to end-June operating results by division, in billions of pesetas unless stated.
NOTE: Repsol said exploration and production results were boosted by the inclusion of Astra and improved operating margins after high value-added production fields were incorporated.
The appreciation of the dollar versus the peseta also boosted results, as did higher crude prices.
Average Brent crude price in the first half was $19.55 per barrel, versus $19.13 in the year-ago period.
Total hydrocarbons output rose to 6.67 million tonnes of petroleum equivalent, up 37.5 percent.
Refining and marketing results were aided by fatter international refining margins, dollar appreciation and Latin American income.

Chemical results were sapped by the stoppage of the Tarragona cracker for maintenance work and a capacity increase, as well as more depreciation because of an asset restatement and the coming on-stream of the new polypropylene unit.
The latter unit, with nominal capacity for 190,000 tonnes production, will allow integration levels to be improved between base and derived petrochemicals in Tarragona, improving competitivity.

A mild winter dented gas division results by about 8.45 billion pesetas and the LPG price freeze reduced profit by roughly 14.7 billion pesetas. Unit margins were also lower because of the spread between purchase and sale prices. Depreciation costs grew because of the asset restatement and the inclusion of the North African gas pipeline.
These negative factors were not compensated, despite increased sales to industry and power stations, Repsol said.
